focus: The advisor cluster: probe battery 13/17 with 2/5 false positives, the path-owner pull, and the never-passed --surface-hint
noveltyJustification: Five new findings: the recorded aggregate and its exact failing probes, the hub-owned-token mechanism behind both negatives and lost positives, the handler call site that omits --surface-hint with the engine fallback it causes, the complete-but-unadopted hint capability, and the scoping decision that leaves the battery unowned.
keyQuestions: Q6: Why does the advisor battery score 13 of 17 with false positives where a file path in the prompt pulls routing, and why does the advisor never pass --surface-hint?
answeredQuestions: Q6: Why does the advisor battery score 13 of 17 with false positives where a file path in the prompt pulls routing, and why does the advisor never pass --surface-hint?
ruledOut: An intent-beats-artifact scoring mode or path-stripping preprocessor - paths are legitimate targets when they are the work item, and the signal list plus the hint already cover the gap
Re-running the battery in this lineage - the advisor is daemon-backed and can write runtime state outside the write boundary; the phase-002 tsv already records the run

label: The SA-001 battery fails both aggregates and the recorded run matches the brief: 13 of 17 positives won (P1, P4, P11, P15 lost) against a ≥14 floor, and 2 of 5 negatives falsely won by sk-code (N1 0.934, N5 0.861) against a 0 floor; phase 002 recorded the same state as an out-of-scope advisor-accuracy issue and reports the aggregate as a number. Smallest fix: give the aggregate a named owner and rerun the battery after the scoring-input fix.

One mechanism produces both the false positives and most lost positives: hub-owned tokens in the prompt outrank intent tokens. N1 is documented by the battery's own triage (an sk-code SKILL.md edit should go to sk-doc but sk-code wins on the mention), and the mirror shows on the positive side: P11 names a system-spec-kit path and system-spec-kit wins, P1 names a system-deep-loop path and cli-external wins, N4 names cli-opencode and cli-external wins over sk-doc. Smallest fix: apply the four signals the battery triage already lists and rerun; no new scoring layer.

The advisor never passes --surface-hint: the handler spawns the front door with exactly --hub and --prompt-stdin, while the front door parses --surface-hint and the engine applies it only when present, with its own comment saying a call without it serves exactly the compiled order; that order is the tieBreak detection precedence OPENCODE > OBSIDIAN > WEBFLOW. The round-four session-aware child recorded that no shipped caller passes the hint yet and named this handler. Smallest fix: pass the detected session surface as one extra argument at the single existing subprocess call site.

The hint capability is complete and tested, so the gap is adoption not construction: the front door accepts the flag, the sk-code canary router implements applySurfaceHint (reorder only among matched surface targets), and compiled-route-surface-hint.test.cjs exercises ordering with 6 of 6 passing per the merge record; the advisor already spawns the front door per eligible recommendation, so the argument adds no process or dependency.

Phase 002's decision D5 correctly kept the battery out of scope (each probe judged against its own before-result, the aggregate reported only as a number), but a known-red suite with no named owner repeats the stale-canary class from iteration 3; the synthesis should attach the owner and the rerun command when the aggregate is reported.
